name: Gyromechanic Gear
summary: Outside Gnomeregan, salvaged Gyromechanic Gears are sought for a bold gnomish experiment. Inventors in Kharanos hope to use them to reverse leper gnome mutations.

sections.title: Components for Recombobulation
sections.body: Radiation swept through Gnomeregan as gnomes fought to purge the trogg invasion. Many survivors became mad, irradiated leper gnomes. Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket refuse to abandon their twisted kin, and have drawn up plans for the ambitious Recombobulator, a contraption meant to undo radiation's effects. Its prototype needs precise mechanisms that can withstand volatile pressure inside the machine, including Gyromechanic Gears and Restabilization Cogs. With local manufacturing gone after the fall of their capital, the inventors must salvage these delicate parts from hostile leper gnomes roaming Dun Morogh.

faq.q: What is a Gyromechanic Gear used for?
faq.answer: Razzle Sprysprocket in Kharanos needs Gyromechanic Gears as core mechanical parts for the Recombobulator. Along with Restabilization Cogs, they will go into the prototype machine designed to cure irradiated leper gnomes.

faq.q: Where do these gears come from?
faq.answer: The gears are salvaged from Leper Gnomes outside Gnomeregan and from Gibblewilt in Dun Morogh.

faq.q: Can the Recombobulator actually cure leper gnomes?
faq.answer: Razzle Sprysprocket trusts Ozzie's schematics and believes adjustments to combustion pistons and electrogum gel can restore their kin. Whether the machine can reverse catastrophic radiation poisoning on a wide scale remains untested.

faq.q: Why can't gnomes simply forge new gears?
faq.answer: The fall of Gnomeregan shattered gnomish industry and left its most sophisticated tools, workshops, and automated foundries out of reach. Salvaging intact pre-fall precision hardware around the city's perimeter is often faster than machining parts by hand.

angles.text: As a gnome, each salvaged gear brings tinkerers closer to a chance of rescuing their radioactive kin wandering the snows outside Gnomeregan.
As an engineer, you know gnomish precision work for its intricate design and tight-tolerance gyromechanic parts, which regulate unstable prototype machinery.
